title: Why we roast in small batches
excerpt: Bigger batches are more efficient. They're also why so much coffee tastes like nothing in particular.
content: Bigger batches are more efficient. They're also why so much coffee tastes like nothing in particular. A five-kilo batch lets us taste and adjust between roasts in a way a hundred-kilo drum never allows. It costs more per bag. We think it's worth it.

title: A note on our Honduras lot
excerpt: This year's lot from the Marcala region came in brighter than usual — here's what changed.
content: This year's lot from the Marcala region came in brighter than usual. The farm shifted part of their drying process to raised beds, which shows up as a cleaner acidity in the cup. We're running it as a light roast through the end of the season.

title: What water actually does to your coffee
excerpt: Most home brewing advice skips the one variable that changes everything else.
content: Most home brewing advice skips the one variable that changes everything else: water. Hard water mutes acidity and can taste flat; very soft water can pull out bitterness unevenly. If your coffee tastes different at a friend's house with the same beans and grinder, this is usually why.
